summary: This Sustainability (MDPI, 2020) article by Mariana Hatmanu, Cristina Cautisanu and Mihaela Ifrim from Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi examines how the monetary policy interest rate, the real exchange rate and the Euro area business climate affect Romania's economic growth. Using an ARDL approach with structural break tests, the authors find that short-run growth is negatively influenced by the interest rate and positively by the exchange rate, while the Euro area business climate has mixed effects. The note is mostly the paper's abstract, introduction and literature review, with website navigation boilerplate removed.
one_line: ARDL study of how Romania's interest rate, real exchange rate and Euro area business climate affect its economic growth, with structural breaks.
key_facts: The article was published in Sustainability in 2020, volume 12, issue 7, article 2798, with DOI 10.3390/su12072798.
The authors are Mariana Hatmanu, Cristina Cautisanu and Mihaela Ifrim, affiliated with the Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi.
The study examines the influence of the monetary policy interest rate, the real exchange rate and the business climate in the Euro area on economic growth in Romania.
The method applies a pre-test for structural breaks, traditional unit root tests, unit root tests with structural breaks, and the Bound cointegration test.
The results show that in the short run, economic growth is negatively influenced by the interest rate.
The results show that in the short run, economic growth is positively influenced by the exchange rate.
The Euro area business climate has mixed effects on Romania's economic growth.
The main goal of the National Bank of Romania (NBR) is to ensure and maintain price stability.
The Introduction states that the convergence of Romanian monetary policy with Euro area monetary policy is justified on three levels.
Barsky and Sims identified two distinct perspectives on the role of confidence in macroeconomics.
Hossain's study covered 62 years of economic growth determinants in Bangladesh.
Próchniak and Witkowski analysed the interest rate and economic growth in EU27 countries during 1993–2010 and in EU15 between 1972 and 2010, obtaining mixed and unstable results.
Keywords include economic growth, unit root tests, multiple structural breaks, Bound cointegration test and econometric model.
The paper was submitted on 5 February 2020, revised on 15 March 2020, accepted on 28 March 2020 and published on 1 April 2020.
